messages:
anya: Heads-up — observed a sudden latency/regression on prod runner when the torch.compile + CUDA graph path kicks in. Happens around seqlen transition 384 -> 512, kernel selector flips and KV-cache churn spikes.

matt: ugh, any logs or traces?

anya: pasted a compact trace from the failing run below:

```
# trace snippet
time: 2026-03-10T14:22:11Z
runner-id: r-73
seq_len: 512
path: jit->cudagraphs (dynamic)
kernel_choice: matmul_f32_tiled_v2
autotune_label: arch_amp_v3
kvcache_evicted: true
kv_evict_count: 3
stall_ms: 47
cpu_sched_wait_ms: 5
```

anya: TL;DR kernel went to f32-tiled variant (higher throughput, worse latency for small batches) and we evicted KV pages during capture handshake which added stalls.

lucas: can you repro locally with the microbench? iirc we added a new heuristic in PR#4207 that biases tiled kernels for certain sm architectures.

anya: repro is pretty stable on our staging GPU pool. command I used: `./perf_runner --model llama-13b --jit --cudagraphs --seq-len 512 --batch 1 --profile`

izzy: @lucas @dmitri quick thought — the autotuner recently started including sequence-length buckets that are inclusive on the upper bound; crossing 512 may promote to a different kernel id. Could be an off-by-one in the bucket mapper.

matt: can you dump the kernel_profile and the bucket map? even a CSV is fine.

anya: attaching the two excerpts inline:

```
# kernel_profile.csv
bucket,seq_min,seq_max,kernel_id,latency_us
b1,1,383,mm_small_f16,110
b2,384,511,mm_mid_f16,125
b3,512,1024,matmul_f32_tiled_v2,180
```

```
# bucket_map.json (trimmed)
{
  "buckets": ["b1","b2","b3"],
  "rules": ["inclusive_upper"]
}
```

izzy: yep that mapping explains it. b3 picks matmul_f32_tiled_v2 which hurts single-request latency. We should prefer mm_mid_f16 for batch<=2 even in b3.

dmitri: +1. Also kvcache eviction during graph capture is suspicious — maybe capture memory footprint triggered an eager eviction routine. We should log mem high-water and pin KV cache during capture handshake.

matt: quick mitigation: force kernel override for that model on the problematic SM family. Patch config at runtime: `kernel.overrides["llama-13b"].prefer = ["mm_mid_f16", "mm_small_f16"]` — can we try that on staging?

anya: testing override now on staging pool-7. patch applied. rerunning the same perf command.

perf-bot: Alert: latency SLO breached for r-73 at 2026-03-10T14:22:11Z (p99 452ms > 350ms). Related traces: 7.

anya: after override run: p99 dropped from 452ms -> 128ms, stall_ms -> 6, kv_evict_count -> 0. Looks promising.

lucas: good catch. Next steps: 1) revert inclusive_upper behavior in bucket mapper or make kernel selection aware of batch/kv state; 2) add KV pinning during capture handshake; 3) add small-batch bias for b3 in autotuner. I'll open an RFC/PR with proposals.

izzy: also add a microtest to assert stable kernel choice at boundary seq lengths (e.g., 511 vs 512) for various batch sizes.

anya: filed a quick issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/7892 — includes traces and repro commands.

matt: thanks. If we can get a short rollback/playbook, ops can push the override to prod while we fix autotuner.

dmitri: I'll draft the playbook and a canary rollout plan for override.

anya: thanks team. I'll keep thread updated with additional runs.
